h1: What Corrext is and what it does for you
lead: Answers to the questions people ask before they start: the platform's tools, the LexMachina engine, review, pricing and set-up.
title: Explore Corrext: features and engines · Help Centre · Neur.on
description: What Corrext is, its four tools, the LexMachina engine and the other engines available, review, pricing, trial and set-up.

articles.question: What is Corrext?
articles.reponse: Corrext is Neur.on's legal and financial translation platform. It brings together four tools, all available from the home page. Text and document translation gives you a translation straight away. With Translation projects, you have your documents reviewed and certified. Fast lookup CHnell checks a term in Swiss official texts. Commercial register extracts lets you order a certified translation online.
savoir: Your documents are stored in Switzerland, whichever engine you choose.
Several engines are available, including LexMachina, Neur.on's Swiss engine.

articles.titre: Why the tool names in the app differ from this website
articles.question: Why do the tool names in the app differ from this website?
articles.reponse: The app has its own labels for the tools, and they are not always the names used on this website and in this Help Centre. Here is how they match: ‘Fast translation’ is Text and document translation, ‘Translation project’ is Translation projects, ‘Fast lookup’ is Fast lookup CHnell, and ‘Commercial register extract’ is Commercial register extracts.
savoir: In this Help Centre, labels in bold or in single quotes are exactly as the app displays them.

articles.question: What is LexMachina?
articles.reponse: It is Neur.on's neural machine translation engine. It is trained on Swiss legal and financial data: more than 15 million multilingual segments from Federal Supreme Court case law, FINMA texts and the legal codes. It runs in Switzerland. See the LexMachina page.

articles.titre: Using DeepL or a general-purpose model in Corrext
articles.question: Can I use DeepL or a general-purpose AI model in Corrext?
articles.reponse: Yes. DeepL Pro, Azure OpenAI GPT and Claude are available in the interface, with a pseudonymisation notice that appears when you select one of them. The Alternatives feature compares up to four suggestions, each labelled with the engine that produced it.

articles.question: Who reviews the translations?
articles.reponse: Your own teams, in an internal review. A legal translator, in Light review or Full review. Or two translators and a specialised agency, for Double review & certified translation. You choose the level document by document in the project workflow, and the delivery time is shown before you confirm.

articles.question: How much does it cost?
articles.reponse: Prices are not published: they depend on volumes, languages and the review level. In the app, the quote and the delivery time appear before you confirm anything. They are calculated from the number of standard pages and the legal category detected in your files. Your needs are scoped during a demo.

articles.question: Is there a free trial?
articles.reponse: There is no self-service trial. A specialist gives you a demo on your own documents, in your languages. The interactive demo on this website reproduces the real interface, with results produced in the app.

articles.question: How long does set-up take?
articles.reponse: The web app requires no installation: all you need is an account, with password login or Microsoft single sign-on. Integration with your systems via API, or deployment on your own servers, is scoped in a technical discussion.

h1: Open Corrext and get to know its four tools
lead: Log in, identify the four tools on the home page, choose a translation engine and decide on the confidentiality level: everything you need to know before you translate your first document in Corrext.
title: Getting started with Corrext: log in and translate · Neur.on
description: Open Corrext, identify the four tools on the home page, choose a translation engine and understand the confidentiality mode before you start.

articles.title: Corrext login: password or Microsoft SSO · Neur.on
articles.description: Log in to Corrext with your email address and a password of at least 12 characters, or with your organisation's Microsoft single sign-on.
articles.reponse: Corrext opens from corrext.com, which redirects you to the platform's login page. Log in with your email address and your password, which must be at least 12 characters long, or with the Microsoft single sign-on button if your organisation has enabled it. Once you are logged in, you land on the home page, which lists your translation tools.
etapes: Open corrext.com in your browser: the page redirects you to the platform's login screen.
Enter your work email address, then your password, which has at least 12 characters.
Or click Log in with Microsoft single sign-on to use your organisation's single sign-on.
If you have forgotten your password, click ‘Forgot your password ?’ below the form to start the reset procedure.
You land on the home page, titled ‘Home | Corrext’, where your tools are grouped under ‘My translation tools’.
savoir: Corrext's interface is in English. All the labels quoted in this Help Centre are exactly what you see on screen.
The Microsoft single sign-on button depends on your organisation's settings. If it does not respond, contact your administrator.
The login screen does not let you create an account: your administrator sets up your access.
articles.question: How do I log in to Corrext?

articles.titre: The four tools on the home page
articles.title: The four tools on the Corrext home page · Neur.on
articles.description: Text and document translation, Translation projects, Fast lookup and Commercial register extract: what each of the four home page cards in Corrext does.
articles.reponse: The Corrext home page groups four tools under the heading ‘My translation tools’. Text and document translation (the ‘Fast translation’ card) translates a text or files immediately. Translation projects (the ‘Translation project’ card) estimates a delivery time and lets you order a review. Fast lookup searches for a term in context in CHnell. Commercial register extract lets you order a certified translation of a commercial register extract. Your current projects appear further down, under ‘My projects’.
etapes: Log in: the home page appears straight after login, or via the ‘Home’ link in the header.
Find the My translation tools section: it contains four cards, each with an arrow button on the right.
Choose Fast translation (Text and document translation on this website) to translate a text or files straight away, compare alternatives and rephrase.
Choose Translation project (Translation projects on this website) to estimate a review time, get a quote and order an external review.
Choose Fast lookup to search for a term in context and find synonyms in the CHnell tool.
Choose Commercial register extract to order a certified translation, with notarisation and an apostille if needed.
Scroll down to My projects to find your projects. Until you have one, the screen offers ‘Create project’.
savoir: The app uses its own labels: ‘Fast translation’ corresponds to Text and document translation, and ‘Translation project’ to Translation projects, the names used on this website.
The ‘Commercial register extract’ card opens a separate online service: you leave the Corrext interface.
The header is the same on every screen: the Corrext logo, the ‘Home’ link, the notification bell and an avatar with your initials.
Fast lookup works on its own, but also from a translation in progress: highlighting a word opens a search for that word in context.
articles.question: What are the four tools on the home page?

articles.title: How to choose a translation engine in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: Corrext lets you choose the translation engine: LexMachina, Neur.on's Swiss engine, or third-party engines hosted abroad. Here is what your choice changes.
articles.reponse: In Text and document translation, a drop-down list to the right of the languages lets you choose the engine that translates your text or files. It offers LexMachina, Neur.on's Swiss engine, and third-party engines hosted abroad: ‘DeepL Pro’, ‘Azure OpenAI GPT’ and ‘Claude’. If you choose a third-party engine, an Attorney-Client privilege notice appears, and you must read it before sending anything.
etapes: Open Text and document translation from the home page, then stay on the ‘Text translation’ tab or switch to ‘File translation’.
Find the engine drop-down list in the settings bar, to the right of the two language lists.
Open it and choose a Swiss Neur.on engine to keep processing in Switzerland.
Or choose a third-party engine (‘DeepL Pro’, ‘Azure OpenAI GPT’ or ‘Claude’) to compare another way of translating.
Read the Attorney-Client privilege notice if it appears: it requires you to pseudonymise the document before sending it.
On the ‘File translation’ tab, you choose the engine together with the target language, under ‘Choose a translation engine and a target language’.
savoir: The ‘Alternatives’ panel lets you compare several engines on the same sentence without changing your main setting.
The engine you choose does not change where your data is stored: it stays on servers in Switzerland. It changes where the data is processed.
articles.question: How do I choose a translation engine?

articles.title: Corrext Highly sensitive content mode explained · Neur.on
articles.description: What the Highly sensitive content toggle changes: storage and processing in Switzerland, no reuse in translation memory, four languages available.
articles.reponse: ‘Highly sensitive content’ mode ensures that your data is stored and processed exclusively in Switzerland, and that the translated content does not feed into any translation memory for your future projects. In Text and document translation, it is a toggle to the right of the tabs. In Translation projects, it is one of the two confidentiality cards. It is available for German, French, Italian and English.
etapes: In Text and document translation, find the Highly sensitive content toggle, to the right of the row of tabs.
Switch it on before you enter your text or upload your files: it stays on when you move to the ‘File translation’ tab.
Check your target language: in sensitive mode, only EN, FR, IT and DE are offered.
In Translation projects, when asked ‘How confidential are the project and the uploaded files?’, choose the Highly sensitive content card.
Continue through the workflow as usual: the confidentiality setting applies to every file in the project.
savoir: On the ‘PDF to Word’ tab, the toggle is greyed out: PDF to Word conversion is not available in this mode.
In sensitive mode, no content is reused as translation memory. With standard confidentiality, your projects feed your own memory, which only you can use.
If your target language disappears from the list, sensitive mode is restricting it: switch the mode off or choose one of the four available languages.
articles.question: What does Highly sensitive content mode do?

articles.title: The Attorney-Client privilege notice in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: Why Corrext displays a notice when you choose a third-party engine hosted abroad, and what your organisation requires before you send anything.
articles.reponse: When you select a third-party translation engine hosted abroad, Corrext displays an ‘Attorney-Client privilege notice’ banner. It reminds you of your organisation's rule: remove from the document any reference that could reveal the identity of clients or related parties, or the subject of the matter. These engines may only be used for fully pseudonymised documents, and never for a sensitive or high-profile matter.
etapes: Open the engine list in Text and document translation and select a third-party engine, for example ‘DeepL Pro’.
Read the Attorney-Client privilege notice banner that appears above the work area.
Remove client names, related parties and anything that could identify the matter from your text or files.
Do not use these engines for a high-profile or price-sensitive matter: your organisation prohibits it.
If pseudonymisation is not possible, go back to a Swiss Neur.on engine or switch on ‘Highly sensitive content’ mode.
savoir: The notice is an organisational rule applied in the tool, not just an information message: you are responsible for complying with it.
The engines concerned are the third-party engines: ‘DeepL Pro’, ‘Azure OpenAI GPT’ and ‘Claude’. LexMachina, Neur.on's Swiss engine, does not trigger this notice.
Storage stays in Switzerland whatever the engine. It is the processing, that is, sending the text to the engine, that leaves Switzerland.
articles.question: What does the Attorney-Client privilege notice mean?

articles.title: Choose source and target languages in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: Automatic detection of the source language, swapping languages, the 30 target languages of the platform and its four native languages.
articles.reponse: Corrext offers 30 target languages on the platform, with German, French, Italian and English as its four native languages. The source language is detected automatically: the left-hand list shows ‘Detect language’, then the recognised language as soon as you start typing. A swap button between the two lists switches the source and target languages in one click.
etapes: Open Text and document translation: the left-hand list shows Detect language by default.
Start typing your text: the list switches to the recognised language, which you can correct manually.
Open the right-hand list to choose your target language. English is selected by default.
Use the swap button between the two lists to switch the source and target languages.
If the language you need is missing, check the ‘Highly sensitive content’ toggle: it restricts the choice to EN, FR, IT and DE.
savoir: If the source and target languages are the same, the right-hand pane shows ‘Identical source and target languages’ instead of a translation.
In Translation projects, you choose target languages with the ‘Select target languages’ button, which lets you select several languages at once.
In CHnell, you set the language pair at the top of the screen, with the same two lists and swap button.
articles.question: Which languages can I use?

h1: Translate, convert and rephrase straight away
lead: Text and document translation has four tabs: text translation, file translation, PDF to Word conversion and rephrasing. Here is exactly what to do on each one, and how to compare engines on the same sentence.
title: Text and document translation in Corrext · Neur.on
description: Translate a text, upload up to 25 files, convert a PDF to Word, compare engines and rephrase: the basic steps, one at a time.

articles.title: Translate a text in Corrext, step by step · Neur.on
articles.description: Paste a text into Text and document translation, choose the languages and the engine, and read the translation as you type, up to 10,000 characters.
articles.reponse: In Text and document translation, the ‘Text translation’ tab translates as you type: there is no button to press. Text pasted into the left-hand pane is translated in the right-hand pane, up to the limit of 10,000 characters shown by the counter below the input area. A copy button at the top of the right-hand pane retrieves the result.
etapes: Open Text and document translation from the home page, then stay on the Text translation tab.
Check the Highly sensitive content toggle and the engine, on the right of the settings bar.
Leave the left-hand list on ‘Detect language’ or set the source language, then choose the target language on the right.
Paste or type your text in the left-hand pane: the translation appears in the right-hand pane without any action on your part.
Watch the counter below the input area: it shows how many of the 10,000 characters you have used.
Click the copy button at the top right of the target pane to retrieve the translation.
savoir: Each pane has its own undo and redo buttons below the text area, and the source pane also has a clear button.
The sparkle button at the bottom right of the target pane opens the ‘Alternatives’ panel and its competing versions.
To check a specific word, highlight it in the source pane: a ‘Fast Lookup’ button appears and opens CHnell on that word in context.
articles.question: How do I translate a text?

articles.title: Translate several files at once in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: Upload up to 25 Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files of up to 50 MB each to Text and document translation, with the engine and target language you choose.
articles.reponse: The ‘File translation’ tab of Text and document translation translates your documents without copying and pasting. First choose an engine and a target language, then upload up to 25 files, each up to 50 MB, in .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt or .pptx format. The ‘Highly sensitive content’ toggle stays active on this tab, so you can process a confidential batch without it leaving Switzerland.
etapes: Open Text and document translation, then click the File translation tab.
Under Choose a translation engine and a target language, set the engine, then the target language.
Check the ‘Highly sensitive content’ toggle if your documents are confidential: it also applies to files.
Click the Click to upload or drag and drop area, or drag your files onto it.
Stay within the limits shown: up to 25 files, 50 MB per file, in .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt and .pptx format.
Wait until each file has been processed before you leave the tab.
savoir: Where you can, always use the original format (.docx or .xlsx rather than PDF): the layout is better preserved.
A scan or a non-editable PDF should go through the ‘PDF to Word’ tab first, which makes it editable.
To have your files reviewed by a legal translator, use Translation projects rather than Text and document translation.
articles.question: How do I translate Word, Excel or PDF files?

articles.title: Convert a PDF to Word with the PDF to Word tab · Neur.on
articles.description: The PDF to Word tab turns up to 25 PDF files of up to 50 MB into editable Word documents, ready for translation, annotation or legal review.
articles.reponse: The ‘PDF to Word’ tab of Text and document translation converts your PDFs, including scanned documents, into editable Word files. It accepts up to 25 files in .pdf format, each up to 50 MB. This is the first step when a document only exists as a PDF and you then want to translate it, annotate it or have it properly reviewed.
etapes: Open Text and document translation, then click the PDF to Word tab.
Click the upload area or drag your files onto it: only .pdf files are accepted on this tab.
Stay within the limits shown: up to 25 files, 50 MB per file.
Download the converted Word documents, then check the layout before you use them.
Go back to ‘File translation’ if you then want to translate the converted documents.
savoir: The ‘Highly sensitive content’ toggle is greyed out on this tab: it does not apply to PDF to Word conversion.
When the original file exists in .docx or .xlsx, use it directly: converting from a PDF is still a reconstruction.
Conversion does not translate: it makes the document editable. You then translate it on another tab or in a project.
articles.question: How do I convert a PDF to Word?

articles.title: Compare alternatives by engine in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: The Alternatives panel offers several translations of the same sentence, each labelled with the engine that produced it, and a Generate more button.
articles.reponse: Corrext does not stop at one translation. The sparkle button at the bottom right of the target pane opens an ‘Alternatives’ panel with several versions of the same sentence. Each alternative shows the name of the engine that produced it, so you can compare wordings before you choose. A pager scrolls through the suggestions, and a ‘Generate more’ button asks for new ones.
etapes: First translate a text in the ‘Text translation’ tab of Text and document translation.
Click the sparkle button at the bottom right of the target pane.
Read the Alternatives panel that opens below the translation: each suggestion is followed by the name of its engine.
Use the pager arrows, to the right of the suggestion counter, to move from one alternative to the next.
Click Generate more to get other wordings if none of them is suitable.
Copy the version you choose with the copy button of the target pane.
savoir: Labelling each alternative with its engine is the whole point of the panel: it shows where engines diverge on a legal term.
A brief error message may appear before the panel loads. Run the generation again: the panel then fills up.
Comparing alternatives does not replace human review: for a binding document, use Translation projects.
articles.question: How do I compare translations from several engines?

articles.titre: Launch Fast Lookup from a translation
articles.title: Launch Fast Lookup from a Corrext translation · Neur.on
articles.description: Highlight a word in Text and document translation and a Fast Lookup button appears: it opens CHnell on that word, in context, without leaving your translation.
articles.reponse: When you are unsure about a word in Text and document translation, highlight it: a floating ‘Fast Lookup’ button appears just above the selection. It opens the CHnell tool on that exact word, with bilingual segments taken from official Swiss sources. It is the quickest way to check the meaning or usage of a term without leaving your translation.
etapes: Translate your text in the ‘Text translation’ tab of Text and document translation.
Double-click the word you want to check in the source pane, or select it with the mouse.
Click the floating Fast Lookup button that appears above the selection.
In CHnell, read the bilingual segments that contain this word, with their domain and their source.
Go back to your translation and correct the term if official usage differs from the engine's suggestion.
savoir: The help banner below the tool describes exactly this: highlight the chosen word, then click ‘Fast Lookup’.
Fast Lookup also works on its own, from the ‘Fast lookup’ card on the home page, when you start from a term rather than a translation.
The results come from public Swiss sources, with the name of the source below each segment: you can cite the usage, not just assume it.
articles.question: How do I check a term without leaving my translation?

articles.title: Rephrase a text with Rephrasing in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: The Rephrasing tab rewrites a text of up to 5,000 characters in one of five styles, including Formal legal and Simplified, with an option to shorten it.
articles.reponse: The ‘Rephrasing’ tab of Text and document translation rewrites a text in the style you choose, without changing the language. It accepts up to 5,000 characters. A ‘Settings’ list gives access to five styles, including ‘Formal legal’ and ‘Simplified’, and to a ‘Shorten’ option that shortens the text. The words that have changed are underlined in the result.
etapes: Open Text and document translation, then click the Rephrasing tab.
Paste your text into the left-hand pane: the counter shows how many of the 5,000 characters you have used.
Open the Settings list and choose a style: ‘Formal legal’, ‘Financial’, ‘Simplified’, ‘Formal’ or ‘Informal’.
Tick the Shorten option if you also want to shorten the text, then click ‘Apply’.
Read the result in the right-hand pane: the words that have changed are underlined.
Click the regenerate button at the bottom right of the target pane if the rephrasing is not suitable.
Click ‘Reset’ in ‘Settings’ to go back to the default settings.
savoir: A coloured dot next to ‘Settings’ shows that a setting is active: it is the quickest way to see that a style still applies.
The limit of 5,000 characters is specific to rephrasing. Text translation accepts 10,000 characters.
The ‘Simplified’ style deliberately produces a shorter, more direct text: review it before you send it to anyone else.
articles.question: How do I rephrase a text?

articles.titre: Correct, copy and clear a translation
articles.title: Correct, copy and clear a Corrext translation · Neur.on
articles.description: Undo, redo, clear the input area and copy the translation: the controls of the two panes of Text and document translation, and what each one does.
articles.reponse: Both panes of Text and document translation have their own controls. Below each text area, an undo button and a redo button reverse your changes. The source pane has a cross that clears the input, and a character counter. The target pane has a copy button at the top right and, at the bottom right, the alternatives or regenerate button, depending on the tab.
etapes: Find the undo and redo buttons below each pane: they work separately on the source and on the target.
Click the cross in the source pane to clear the input area completely and start again with a new text.
Watch the character counter in the source pane: it shows the limit of the current tab.
Click the copy button at the top right of the target pane to copy the translation to the clipboard.
Use the button at the bottom right of the target pane to open the alternatives, or to regenerate a rephrasing.
savoir: Clearing the source pane also clears the target pane: the translation updates as you type, with no confirm button.
The target pane is not a free editing area: to rework a text, use the ‘Rephrasing’ tab.
If the target pane shows ‘Identical source and target languages’, change the target language: nothing is translated while it is the same as the source.
articles.question: How do I correct, copy or clear a translation?

h1: Get a translation reviewed and quoted
lead: Translation projects takes you through three ordering steps (project set-up, file overview and quotes), then terminology, engine choice and review in the editor. Here is how to create a project, set your terms, review the translation and approve it.
title: Translation projects: Corrext review and quotes · Neur.on
description: Create a project, set the terminology, choose the engine, review in the editor or in Word, get a quote and approve the translation.

articles.title: Create a new translation project in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: Name a project, keep the default name and choose the target languages: the first step of the Translation projects workflow, explained screen by screen.
articles.reponse: Translation projects runs in three steps shown at the top of the screen: ‘Set-up’, ‘File overview’ and then ‘Quotes’. The first step asks for a project name, a confidentiality level and one or more target languages. The ‘Next’ button stays inactive until you choose a target language. The project is created as soon as you move to the next step.
etapes: Open Translation projects from the home page: the Set-up step appears first.
Enter a name in Project name, or leave the ‘Use default name’ toggle on: it builds a name from the date, the organisation and the user.
Answer the question ‘How confidential are the project and the uploaded files?’ by choosing one of the two confidentiality cards.
Click Select target languages and tick your target languages in the list, using the search field if needed.
Check the language tags shown below the button: you can remove each one by clicking its cross.
Click Next, which becomes active as soon as you select a target language.
savoir: The project is created when you move to the ‘File overview’ step: it then has its own address.
You can select several target languages for the same project: the quote then shows them file by file.
The settings button at the bottom of the workflow showed nothing when the app was audited: its function is not documented here.
articles.question: How do I create a translation project?

articles.titre: What the Set-up step asks for
articles.question: What does the Set-up step ask me for?
articles.reponse: The project name, the target languages and the confidentiality level, then two further questions: one related to insider trading, the other about translating the comments in the document.
savoir: The target languages cannot be changed once the project has been created: check them before you move to the next step.
The confidentiality level applies to every file in the project.

articles.title: Choose the confidentiality level of a project · Neur.on
articles.description: Standard confidentiality or Highly sensitive content: where your data is processed, and which of the two modes feeds your translation memory.
articles.reponse: At the ‘Set-up’ step, Corrext asks you to choose between two cards. ‘Standard confidentiality’ saves the project on Corrext's Swiss servers and processes it in or outside Switzerland, depending on the engine you choose. The project can then serve as a translation memory, for you alone. ‘Highly sensitive content’ stores and processes the project exclusively in Switzerland, with no reuse in memory, for German, French, Italian and English.
etapes: At the Set-up step, find the question ‘How confidential are the project and the uploaded files?’
Choose Standard confidentiality for an everyday project: storage on Corrext's Swiss servers, processing according to the engine you choose.
Choose Highly sensitive content for a confidential matter: storage and processing exclusively in Switzerland.
Check your languages: in sensitive mode, only EN, FR, IT and DE are available.
Continue through the workflow: your choice applies to all the files uploaded to the project.
savoir: With standard confidentiality, projects are kept on Corrext's Swiss servers and can be reused as translation memory by you alone.
In sensitive mode, no translated content feeds into a translation memory for future projects.
The confidentiality setting is no substitute for care in choosing the engine: a third-party engine hosted abroad triggers the Attorney-Client privilege notice.
articles.question: Which confidentiality level should I choose for a project?

articles.titre: Upload the files and check the detection
articles.title: Upload and check the files of a project · Neur.on
articles.description: At the File overview step, Corrext counts the standard pages and detects the language and category of each file: check them before you continue.
articles.reponse: The second step, ‘File overview’, accepts your documents in .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt and .pptx format, up to 50 MB each. Each uploaded file shows its name, its number of standard pages, its detected language and its detected legal category, for example 2.5 standard pages for a short document. You can change the language and the category: check them, because the quote is based on them.
etapes: At the File overview step, click the upload area or drag your documents onto it.
Use the original format where possible (.docx or .xlsx rather than PDF), as the upload area advises.
Check the number of standard pages calculated for each file: it is the unit for the quote and the delivery time.
Check Detected language and correct it if the detection was wrong.
Check Detected category, the detected legal category, and adjust it if it does not match the document.
Remove a file with its delete icon, or download it with the icon next to it, then click ‘Next’.
savoir: The ‘Next’ button stays locked until you upload a file: the quotes step needs at least one document.
The detected legal category guides the processing: correcting it at this step avoids a quote based on the wrong area of law.
A scanned PDF should first go through the ‘PDF to Word’ tab of Text and document translation, and then be uploaded in Word format.
articles.question: How do I upload files and check the detected language and category?

articles.titre: How a standard page is calculated
articles.question: How is a standard page calculated?
articles.reponse: A standard page has 1,800 characters, including spaces. Corrext counts the standard pages of each file at the File overview step. This unit, together with the detected legal category, is used for the quote and the delivery time.
savoir: Two short documents can add up to fewer standard pages than a single dense document.

articles.titre: Choose between internal review and a custom workflow
articles.title: Internal review or custom workflow in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: At the Quotes step, Corrext offers two options: put a value on your own review, or order an external review file by file, with a due date.
articles.reponse: The third step, ‘Quotes’, opens on two tab cards. ‘Internal review’ estimates the time needed for the review you carry out yourselves and ends with the ‘Create project’ button. ‘Custom workflow’ adds an external review: you set a due date, an order of priority and, for each file, an internal or external review type and a level. The button then becomes ‘Generate quote’.
etapes: At the Quotes step, choose the Internal review card if you review the machine translation yourself.
Fill in the ‘Internal review specifications’ block: the number of standard pages to review and the price per standard page you charge.
Read the ‘Estimated time’ box, which sums up the estimated review time, then click Create project.
Or choose the Custom workflow card to entrust the review to a legal translator or an agency.
Set a due date in ‘Due date’: the calendar greys out weekends and an estimated review time appears.
Answer the question on the order of priority for processing the files, then set up the file table: the File, Languages, Review and Review level columns.
Click Generate quote, which becomes active once you have entered a due date and a review level.
savoir: The price per standard page field in the internal review is used to put a value on your own work in the estimate: the figure is yours to set.
In the file table, the ‘Review’ column distinguishes ‘External’ and ‘Internal’: a single project can mix both.
The ‘Contact us for an earlier delivery date’ link lets you request an earlier due date than the one offered.
articles.question: Internal review or custom workflow: which should I choose?

articles.titre: Understand the three levels of external review
articles.title: The three external review levels in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: Light review, Full review and Double review & certified translation: what each level actually corrects, and which use of the document it suits.
articles.reponse: Corrext offers three levels of external review. ‘Light review’ corrects major errors, omissions and mistranslations, so that you can understand the document and circulate it internally. ‘Full review’ adds consistency, idiomatic usage, style and tone, for a document intended for third parties. ‘Double review’ has the translation reviewed by two legal translators and adds a certificate of accuracy.
etapes: At the ‘Quotes’ step, switch to the Custom workflow card and scroll down to the file table.
Open the Review level column for the file concerned: the three levels are offered there.
Choose Light review, carried out by a legal translator, for a document intended for understanding and internal circulation.
Choose Full review, also carried out by a legal translator, for a document to be shared with third parties.
Choose Double review & certified translation, carried out by a specialised agency, for legal use, publication or filing with an authority.
Hover over the information icon next to a level to read its exact definition in the app.
savoir: The ‘Double review’ certificate is signed by the specialised translation agency in charge of the project. It attests to the accuracy and impartiality of the translation.
You choose the level file by file: a project can combine a ‘Light review’ of exhibits and a ‘Full review’ of a contract.
For a commercial register extract to be filed with an authority, use the dedicated certified translation service instead.
articles.question: What do the three levels of external review cover?

articles.titre: Get a quote and a delivery time
articles.title: Get a quote and delivery time in a Corrext project · Neur.on
articles.description: Corrext calculates the quote and the delivery time from the number of standard pages and the detected category, then breaks down preparation and review.
articles.reponse: At the ‘Quotes’ step, Corrext calculates an estimate from the number of standard pages in your files and the detected legal category. An ‘Estimated time’ box breaks down the preparation time, the internal review time and the external review time, and shows a total cost excluding tax. The ‘Generate quote’ button produces the quote once you have entered the due date and the review level.
etapes: First check, at the ‘File overview’ step, the number of standard pages and the detected category of each file.
At the Quotes step, choose the card that matches your needs: ‘Internal review’ or ‘Custom workflow’.
Enter the due date in ‘Due date’ and the review level of each file: the estimate updates.
Read the Estimated time box: it shows preparation, internal review and external review separately.
Check the total cost excluding tax shown below the estimate before you go any further.
Click Generate quote for the quote of a custom workflow, or Create project for an internal review.
savoir: The unit of calculation is the standard page, not the file: two short documents can add up to less than a single dense document.
The cost shown excludes tax. Corrext states this explicitly in the estimate box.
‘Generate quote’ sends the request to the agency in charge of the external review: only click it when your settings are final.
articles.question: How do I get a quote and a delivery time?

articles.title: Set the terminology of a Corrext project · Neur.on
articles.description: Once the project is created, Corrext identifies the key terms in your documents. Set their translation: the machine translation will then use it.
articles.reponse: Once the project has been created, the ‘Project terminology’ screen shows the terms Corrext has identified in your documents, for example ‘résiliation’ (termination) or ‘for exclusif’ (exclusive jurisdiction). Clicking a term opens a field where you enter its translation in each target language. You can also add your own terms with ‘Custom term’. The project's machine translation uses the translations you set here exactly as they are.
etapes: Click Create project at the ‘Quotes’ step: the Project terminology screen opens.
Browse the suggested terms, grouped under the tab of the source language.
Click a term, for example ‘résiliation’ (termination), to add it to the project terminology.
Enter its translation in the field of each target language, for example ‘EN’.
Add a term that is not in the list with Custom term, or remove one by clicking the bin icon.
Click Next to move on to the choice of engine.
savoir: The translation you set applies to the exact form of the term. A related word, such as the verb ‘résilier’ (to terminate), is not affected.
The suggested terms come from your own documents: the list changes from one project to another.
For terminology shared by all projects, your administrator can import a term base in TBX or XML format at organisation level.
articles.question: How do I set the terminology for a project?

articles.title: Choose the translation engine for a Corrext project · Neur.on
articles.description: The last step before translation: choose the project engine, Swiss or third-party. What the cards say, and what your choice changes for your data.
articles.reponse: After the terminology, the ‘Choose a machine translation engine’ screen shows the engines as cards. The recommended Swiss engine is preselected. LexMachina, Neur.on's engine, ensures 100% Swiss processing. Third-party engines display a reminder: your internal policy may require pseudonymisation first. Clicking ‘Next’ starts the machine translation and opens the project dashboard.
etapes: From ‘Project terminology’, click ‘Next’: the Choose a machine translation engine screen appears.
Find the card marked Recommended: it is the preselected Swiss engine.
Read the description on each card: the LexMachina card states ‘100% Swiss Data Processing’.
For a third-party engine (‘DeepL Pro’, ‘Azure OpenAI GPT’ or ‘Claude’), read the reminder about pseudonymisation before you choose it.
Click Next: the translation starts and the project dashboard opens.
savoir: Your administrator can restrict the list of engines allowed for your organisation.
In ‘Highly sensitive content’ mode, only LexMachina, the Swiss engine, remains available.
According to its card, LexMachina, the recommended engine, stays closest to the source text.
articles.question: How do I choose the engine for a project?

articles.titre: How to work on a project as a team
articles.question: How do I work on a project with colleagues?
articles.reponse: The project dashboard has a Team block, which manages the people working on the project. In the editor, the ‘Sync’ tab of the side panel then brings everyone's work together: version conflicts, incoming changes from a colleague and propagation decisions on repeated segments.
savoir: Propagation decisions apply a correction to identical segments, segment by segment, once you have made your choice.

h1: Review, correct and approve a translation
lead: The review editor opens from a project with ‘Open in CAT’. You review segment by segment, with translation memory, CHnell and the alternatives to hand, then you validate the file and download it.
title: Review editor: revise a translation · Help Centre · Neur.on
description: Review a file in the Corrext editor, use the side panel, work in Word, let the memory learn, then validate and download the translation.

articles.titre: Review a file in the editor
articles.title: Review a translation in the Corrext editor · Neur.on
articles.description: The ‘Open in CAT’ button opens the review editor: source and translation side by side, sentence by sentence, with confirmation and progress tracking.
articles.reponse: On the project dashboard, the ‘Open in CAT’ button opens the review editor. The document is shown in two columns, source text on the left and translation on the right, sentence by sentence. You correct the translation in the right-hand column, confirm each sentence you have reviewed and use the side panel for help: memories, Fast Lookup, AI assistant and Sync.
etapes: Open the project from ‘My projects’ on the home page, then find the file's row in the task table.
Click Open in CAT: the editor opens on the translated document.
Find a word with Filter source or Filter target.
Click a sentence: the side panel shows the memory matches and the AI assistant's alternatives.
Correct the translation in the right-hand column, then tick the sentence's box to confirm it.
Follow the progress as a percentage at the top of the editor, then go back to the dashboard with Back.
savoir: The ‘MT’ marker shows a sentence produced by machine translation. Its gauge gives an indication of quality.
Repeated sentences and tags that do not match between source and translation are flagged in the table.
With standard confidentiality, your corrections enrich your translation memory and are used in your next projects.
articles.question: How do I review a file in the editor?

articles.title: Memories, Fast Lookup, AI and Sync in the editor · Neur.on
articles.description: The editor's side panel brings together memories, Fast Lookup, the AI assistant and Sync. What each tab does and how to use it on a sentence.
articles.reponse: The editor's side panel brings together four tools, available from the icons on the right of the screen: translation memories, Fast Lookup, the AI assistant and Sync. They work on the selected sentence and change nothing until you click ‘Apply’.
etapes: Select a sentence in the editor.
Translation memories tab: look up previously validated translations similar to the sentence, and apply one with ‘Apply’.
Fast Lookup tab: search for a word in the memories and in CHnell, on the ‘Source’ or the ‘Target’ side.
AI Assistant tab, ‘Alternatives’ section: compare the sentence as translated by several engines, and get more with ‘Generate more’.
Rephrasing section: choose a style in ‘Settings’ (Formal legal, Financial, Simplified, Formal, Informal) or the ‘Shorten’ option, then click ‘Apply’.
Sync tab: resolve version conflicts and decide on propagation.
savoir: In Fast Lookup, the term you search for is highlighted in the source and in the translation, with the name of the original document.
Rephrasing underlines the words it changes: you see the difference before you apply it.
Sync is only useful if several people are working on the same file, or if you have opened it in several sessions.
articles.question: What is the editor's side panel for?

articles.titre: Are my corrections used in later translations
articles.question: Are my corrections used in future translations?
articles.reponse: Yes, with Standard confidentiality. The segments you correct and confirm in the editor enrich your organisation's translation memory. Corrext then suggests these matches for similar sentences in later projects: the translation gradually adapts to your vocabulary. In Highly sensitive content mode, nothing is reused.
savoir: Memory matches appear in the ‘Translation memories’ tab of the side panel, with an ‘Apply’ button.
The memory is used exclusively by your organisation.

articles.title: Review a Corrext translation in Word · Neur.on
articles.description: Export the project file, review it in Word with the Corrext add-in (AI assistant, Fast Lookup, memories, Sync), then reimport it into the project.
articles.reponse: If you prefer to review in Word, export the file from the dashboard with ‘Export docx’, open it in Word and display the Corrext add-in from the ribbon. Its panel includes the AI assistant, Fast Lookup, memory matches and Sync. When you have finished reviewing, reimport the file into the project with ‘Reimport docx’.
etapes: On the project dashboard, click Export docx for the file you want to review.
Open the exported file in Word, then click the Corrext button on the ribbon to display the ‘Corrext editor’ panel.
Click Log in if the panel asks you to sign in.
Review with the help of the ‘AI Assistant’, ‘Fast Lookup’, ‘Matches’ and ‘Sync’ tabs.
Save the document, then reimport it into the project with Reimport docx.
savoir: The add-in only opens on a document exported with ‘Export docx’: a file from Text and document translation is rejected.
You must be a member of the project and have Word 2021 or Microsoft 365.
While a long document is loading, do not close the panel or the file. You can already start working, then resolve conflicts in ‘Sync’.
articles.question: How do I review a translation in Word?

articles.title: Validate and download a Corrext translation · Neur.on
articles.description: The ‘Validate’ button closes the review of a file, with no way back. The preview, the Word export and the TMX memory are available from the dashboard.
articles.reponse: When the review is finished, the ‘Validate’ button on the dashboard closes the task: this action is final. The dashboard also offers a preview of the file (‘Preview’), the Word export and a download of the project memory in TMX format.
etapes: Check the progress shown in the editor, then go back to the dashboard.
Check how the file looks with Preview.
Click Validate below the task's ‘Reviewing’ status, then confirm.
To close all the tasks at once, use Validate all.
Download the translation and, if needed, the project memory with Download TMX.
savoir: Validation cannot be undone: Corrext reminds you of this in the confirmation window.
A task goes through the statuses ‘Reviewing’, ‘Validated’ and then ‘Exported’ once the Word file has been exported.
TMX is the standard exchange format for translation memories: you can reuse it in most translation tools.
articles.question: How do I validate and download the translation?

h1: Check a term in official sources
lead: CHnell is a bilingual concordancer: it shows how a term is actually translated in Swiss official texts, segment by segment, with its source and its domain. Here is how to search, filter and read a result.
title: Fast lookup CHnell: search for a term in context · Neur.on
description: Search for a term in CHnell, use the operators, filter by domain and by source, tell the resource types apart and read a segment in context.

articles.title: Search for a term in Fast lookup CHnell · Neur.on
articles.description: Choose a language pair, enter a word or a phrase and run the CHnell search with the Search button to read aligned segments.
articles.reponse: CHnell searches for a word or a phrase in a language pair and returns bilingual segments taken from official sources. Set the source and target languages at the top of the screen. Enter your term in the ‘Search for a word, an expression, a term’ field, then click the ‘Search’ button. The Enter key does not start the search.
etapes: Open Fast lookup from the home page: the CHnell screen appears with two language lists.
Set the source and target languages. The swap button between the two lists switches them.
Enter your term in the Search for a word, an expression, a term field.
Click the Search button: the Enter key does not start the search.
Read the results header: it shows the term searched, the language and the number of results found.
Browse the aligned segments, source on the left and target on the right, with the term highlighted in each.
savoir: Each language list has a clear cross: use it to start again from an empty language pair.
The ‘Show more results’ button at the bottom of the list loads more segments without running the search again.
From a translation in progress, the same tool opens directly on a highlighted word, with the ‘Fast Lookup’ button.
articles.question: How do I search for a term in CHnell?

articles.title: CHnell search operators explained · Neur.on
articles.description: CHnell lists three supported operators below its search field. Where to find them, how to enter them and where to read their exact syntax.
articles.reponse: Below the search field, CHnell displays ‘Supported search operators’, followed by the three supported operators: straight quotation marks, the hyphen and the word ‘or’. An information icon next to this line gives the details in the app. You type the operators directly in the search field, before you click ‘Search’.
etapes: Open ‘Fast lookup’ and find the Supported search operators line below the search field.
Hover over or click the information icon next to this line to read the exact syntax in the app.
Type your query with the operator you need directly in the search field.
Click Search to run the search, then check the number of results shown in the header.
If the query is too broad, add an operator or use the domain and source filters.
savoir: The app lists the three operators without explaining how to use them on screen. Their full definition is in the information tooltip. It is not reproduced here because it was not observed when the app was audited.
Operators do not replace filters: to restrict results to a domain or a source, use ‘Advanced search’ or the ‘Filters’ panel.
Check the language pair before you conclude that a term has no results: sometimes swapping the languages is enough.
articles.question: Which search operators can I use?

articles.title: Filter a CHnell search by domain and source · Neur.on
articles.description: Advanced search and the Filters panel restrict CHnell results to a resource type, to some of the 30 domains and to specific sources.
articles.reponse: CHnell classifies its segments by legal domain and by source. Before you search, the collapsible ‘Advanced search’ block lets you restrict the resource type. It also lets you tick one or more of the 30 available domains, from company law and arbitration to taxation. On the results page, the ‘Filters’ panel repeats these criteria and adds a selection of sources.
etapes: On the CHnell screen, expand the Advanced search block above the search field.
Set Resource type to limit the search to one type of resource.
Open Domains and tick the domains you need: the list has 30, from banking law to patent law.
Run the search with the ‘Search’ button.
On the results page, expand the Filters panel to adjust the same criteria without entering everything again.
Use Select sources in this panel to keep only certain sources, for example federal texts.
savoir: The domain of each segment is shown in capitals above the text: it is the quickest way to judge whether a result is relevant.
Filtering by source is useful when several authorities use different wording for the same concept.
The full list of 30 domains opens in the app: it covers company law as well as criminal law and taxation.
articles.question: How do I filter by domain and source?

articles.title: Shared and own resources in CHnell · Neur.on
articles.description: The Resource type filter in CHnell distinguishes all resources, shared resources and your own resources. Here is what each one covers.
articles.reponse: In ‘Advanced search’, the ‘Resource type’ filter offers three values: ‘All resources’, ‘Shared resources’ and ‘Own resources’. Shared resources are the text collections available to all CHnell users. Own resources are those linked to your organisation. The filter therefore lets you search either everywhere or only in your organisation's own material.
etapes: Expand Advanced search on the CHnell screen.
Open the Resource type filter and read the three values offered.
Choose All resources to search both the shared collections and your organisation's own collections.
Choose Shared resources to keep only the shared collections, which are useful for citing official usage.
Choose Own resources to search only the resources specific to your organisation.
Run the search with ‘Search’ and check the number of results, which varies widely with this filter.
savoir: Adding and managing own resources could not be observed from a standard user account, so these tasks are not documented here. Ask your administrator.
If ‘Own resources’ returns no results, your organisation probably has no own resources linked to it yet.
Shared resources come from public Swiss texts: their source is shown below each segment, which makes them citable.
articles.question: What is the difference between shared resources and own resources?

articles.title: Show a CHnell segment in its context · Neur.on
articles.description: Reading a CHnell result: the aligned segment, the highlighted term, the domain, the official source and the Show in context link below each segment.
articles.reponse: Each CHnell result is an aligned segment: the source sentence on the left and its translation on the right, with the searched term highlighted in both. The legal domain appears above it in capitals, and the exact source of the text below it, for example a federal compilation or an authority's website. The ‘Show in context’ link opens the segment in its original setting, so you can check that it really matches your case.
etapes: Run a search in CHnell and browse the list of aligned segments.
Find the highlighted term in the source sentence and in the target sentence: this is the match to assess.
Read the domain label in capitals above the segment to check that it belongs to the right field of law.
Read the source line below the segment: it names the original text and the dataset it comes from.
Click Show in context to open the segment in its full context.
Click Show more results at the bottom of the list to load more segments.
savoir: A term can have several correct translations depending on the domain: the domain label, not the number of results, settles the question.
The source reference is what makes a usage citable: note it if you need to justify a terminology choice.
The total number of results is shown in the page header: a high figure suggests filtering rather than reading everything.
articles.question: How do I see a segment in its context?

lead: You order the certified translation of a Swiss commercial register extract online, in four steps. Here is how to find the company, choose the certification level and arrange delivery.
title: Certified commercial register extract translation · Neur.on
description: Order the certified translation of a Swiss commercial register extract: company search, certification level, delivery method and delivery time.

articles.title: Order a certified translation of a register extract · Neur.on
articles.description: Find a company by its name or UID number, choose the target language and order the certified translation of a Swiss commercial register extract.
articles.reponse: You order the certified translation of a Swiss commercial register extract from a dedicated online service, which you reach from the ‘Commercial register extract’ card on the Corrext home page. The process has four steps: find the company by its name or its identification number, choose the certification level, choose the delivery method, then set the delivery time. The service covers more than 30 languages.
etapes: On the Corrext home page, click the Commercial register extract card: a separate online service opens.
Search for the company by its name or by its business identification number (UID).
Select the company you found and choose the target language of the translation.
Choose one of the three certification levels offered.
Choose the delivery method, then the delivery time you need.
Confirm with the Order a translation button, or use Contact us for a specific request.
savoir: The service is designed for official use: translations intended for authorities, banks or publication.
The terminology of the extracts is handled by translation models trained specifically on Swiss commercial register extracts.
The confidentiality of the service relies on ISO 27001 certification, the Swiss Data Protection Act (FADP), the GDPR and Swiss infrastructure.
articles.question: How do I order a certified translation of a commercial register extract?

articles.title: Choose the certification level for an extract · Neur.on
articles.description: Standard, notarised, or notarised and apostilled certification: which level to request, depending on the authority that will receive the document.
articles.reponse: Three certification levels are offered for the translation of a commercial register extract. Standard certification provides a signed and stamped certificate that accompanies the translation. Notarised certification adds the involvement of a Swiss notary. Notarised and apostilled certification also adds the apostille issued by the cantonal State Chancellery under the Hague Apostille Convention, which is required for many uses abroad.
etapes: Once you have found the company, go to the step where you select the certification level.
Choose Standard Corrext Certification for a signed and stamped certificate that accompanies the translation.
Choose Notarized Certification when the receiving authority requires the involvement of a Swiss notary.
Choose Notarized & Apostilled Certification when the document is to be submitted abroad under the Hague Apostille Convention.
If in doubt, ask the recipient which level they require: it determines whether the document will be accepted.
savoir: The level required depends on the receiving authority, not on the language: the same extract may need an apostille in one country and not in another.
The apostille is issued by the State Chancellery: it is added to the notarisation and does not replace it.
For a document that is not a commercial register extract, use Translation projects and its ‘Double review’ level.
articles.question: Which certification level should I choose?

articles.titre: Choose the delivery method and time
articles.title: Choose the delivery method and time for an extract · Neur.on
articles.description: Delivery by email, or by email and on paper, with a standard or express delivery time, in Switzerland or abroad: the last two steps of the order.
articles.reponse: The last two steps of the order cover how the document is delivered. First choose the delivery method: by email only, or by email with a paper copy sent by post or by courier. Then set the delivery time, standard or express, in Switzerland or abroad. A paper copy is essential whenever an original signature, a notarisation or an apostille is required.
etapes: Once you have chosen the certification level, go to the delivery method step.
Choose delivery by email if an electronic version is enough for your recipient.
Choose delivery by email and on paper, by post or by courier, whenever a signed original is required.
Go to the delivery time step and choose between standard and express.
Specify the destination, Switzerland or abroad, which determines the shipping options.
Confirm the order with the Order a translation button.
savoir: A notarisation or an apostille is applied to a paper document: allow time in your schedule for delivery by post or courier.
The express delivery time is also available for international shipments, with the corresponding shipping options.
If you have a specific need, the ‘Contact us’ button lets you ask before you confirm the order.
articles.question: How do I choose the delivery method and delivery time?

h1: What Corrext accepts, and its limits
lead: File formats, number and size of uploads, character limits, available languages: all the platform's limits in one place, as they appear in the app.
title: File formats and languages accepted by Corrext · Neur.on
description: The file formats Corrext accepts, the limits on the number and size of files and on characters, the 30 languages and the four native languages.

articles.title: Which file formats does Corrext accept? · Neur.on
articles.description: Corrext accepts .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt and .pptx files. The PDF to Word tab only accepts PDF. Use the original format where possible.
articles.reponse: Corrext accepts seven file formats for translation: .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt and .pptx. This list applies both to the ‘File translation’ tab of Text and document translation and to the ‘File overview’ step of a translation project. The ‘PDF to Word’ tab is the exception: it only accepts .pdf, since its purpose is to convert that format.
etapes: Check your file's extension before you upload it: .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt or .pptx.
Use the original format where possible, .docx or .xlsx rather than PDF, as the upload area of a project reminds you.
To convert a PDF into an editable Word document, use the PDF to Word tab, which only accepts .pdf.
Convert any file in another format beforehand: the app will not accept it as it is.
Read the text of the upload areas: they show the exact list of formats accepted in each place.
savoir: A document uploaded as a PDF when the Word version exists loses layout quality: the original format is always preferable.
A scanned PDF is not text: convert it to Word before you translate it or have it reviewed.
The list of formats is the same for Text and document translation and for Translation projects: a file rejected by one will be rejected by the other.
articles.question: Which file formats are accepted?

articles.title: File size and number limits in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: Up to 25 files per upload and 50 MB per file: the upload limits of Corrext, in Text and document translation and in a translation project alike.
articles.reponse: The upload areas of Corrext state two limits: up to 25 files per upload, and a maximum of 50 MB per file. They apply to both the ‘File translation’ tab and the ‘PDF to Word’ tab of Text and document translation. The ‘File overview’ step of a translation project also states the limit of 50 MB per file.
etapes: Count your files before you upload them: the limit is 25 files per upload.
Check the size of each file: the limit is 50 MB per file, not for the whole batch.
Split a batch that is too large into several successive uploads rather than forcing a single upload.
Reduce the size of a heavy PDF, or go back to the original Word file, which is often much smaller.
Read the limits shown in the upload area of the current tab or step: they are always displayed there.
savoir: A rejected file is more often due to its format or size than to its content: check these two points first.
For a translation project, the quote is calculated in standard pages: the number of files matters less than how dense they are.
Using the original format often makes the file smaller as well as improving the layout.
articles.question: How many files can I upload, and how large can they be?

articles.title: Character limits in Corrext explained · Neur.on
articles.description: Text translation accepts 10,000 characters and rephrasing 5,000. Beyond that, use file translation rather than splitting your text into pieces.
articles.reponse: Text and document translation has two character limits. The ‘Text translation’ tab accepts 10,000 characters, shown by a counter below the input area. The ‘Rephrasing’ tab stops at 5,000 characters. Beyond that, the right approach is not to keep splitting your text, but to use the ‘File translation’ tab, which handles a whole document.
etapes: Watch the counter below the input area: it shows the number of characters used and the limit of the tab.
Stay below 10,000 characters for a text translation in the ‘Text translation’ tab.
Stay below 5,000 characters for rephrasing in the ‘Rephrasing’ tab.
Beyond that, save your text in a document and upload it to the File translation tab.
For a long document that needs review, open a project in Translation projects instead.
savoir: The counter updates as you type: you can see immediately when pasted text exceeds the limit.
The rephrasing limit is lower than the translation limit: a text you can translate in one go cannot necessarily be rephrased in one go.
Splitting a long text loses the context from one sentence to the next: file translation gives a more consistent result.
articles.question: What are the character limits?

articles.title: Corrext's 30 languages and its native languages · Neur.on
articles.description: Corrext covers 30 target languages, including four native languages, and is limited to German, French, Italian and English in sensitive mode.
articles.reponse: Corrext offers 30 target languages on the platform, from English to Japanese, including Arabic, Chinese, Polish and Turkish. Four of them are native and cover the languages of Swiss legal work: German, French, Italian and English. ‘Highly sensitive content’ mode restricts the choice to these four languages, because processing must then stay in Switzerland.
etapes: Open the target language list in Text and document translation, or the ‘Select target languages’ button in a project.
Use the search field of the list to find a language without scrolling through all 30 entries.
For Swiss legal work, choose one of the four native languages where you can: German, French, Italian or English.
Check the ‘Highly sensitive content’ toggle if a language you expect does not appear: it limits the choice to EN, FR, IT and DE.
In a translation project, tick several target languages at once: each one then appears as a tag.
savoir: The 30 languages cover the main European languages and several Asian languages, as well as both variants of Portuguese and of Chinese.
The difference between a native language and an available language lies in the depth of legal processing, not just in being on the list.
In CHnell, you choose the language pair independently of the one used in your current translation.
articles.question: Which languages are available, and which are native?
Is the layout preserved when I translate a file?
articles.reponse: Yes, the translation is delivered in the original format. For a PDF, especially a scan, the PDF to Word tab first produces an editable Word document.

h1: Where your data goes, and who processes it
lead: Swiss storage, processing that depends on the engine, translation memories, account management: precise answers to the security questions Corrext raises, with no promise beyond what the app shows.
title: Corrext security, privacy and account · Help Centre · Neur.on
description: Where your data is stored and processed, which engines process it outside Switzerland, how memories work and how to manage your account.

articles.titre: Where my data is hosted and processed
articles.title: Where your Corrext data is hosted and processed · Neur.on
articles.description: Storage is in Switzerland in every case. Processing stays in Switzerland in Highly sensitive content mode or with a Swiss Neur.on engine.
articles.reponse: In Corrext, storage and processing are two separate things. Projects are saved on Corrext's Swiss servers in every case. Processing, however, depends on your choice. It stays exclusively in Switzerland in ‘Highly sensitive content’ mode or with a Swiss Neur.on engine. It may take place outside Switzerland if you choose a third-party engine hosted abroad.
etapes: At the ‘Set-up’ step of a project, read the description of the two confidentiality cards: it states the exact rule.
Choose Highly sensitive content so that storage and processing take place exclusively in Switzerland.
Choose Standard confidentiality if processing can follow the engine you choose: storage stays in Switzerland.
In Text and document translation, check the ‘Highly sensitive content’ toggle and the engine before you enter confidential content.
If the Attorney-Client privilege notice appears, the engine you have chosen processes data outside Switzerland.
savoir: The rule to remember: Swiss storage in every case, and exclusively Swiss processing in sensitive mode or with a Swiss Neur.on engine.
Sensitive mode is available for German, French, Italian and English.
The certified translation service for commercial register extracts relies on ISO 27001 certification and Swiss infrastructure.
articles.question: Where is my data hosted and processed?

articles.titre: Which engines process data outside Switzerland
articles.title: Which Corrext engines process data abroad · Neur.on
articles.description: DeepL Pro, Azure OpenAI GPT and Claude are hosted abroad and trigger the Attorney-Client privilege notice. Neur.on's engines stay in Switzerland.
articles.reponse: Corrext distinguishes two families of engines. LexMachina, Neur.on's Swiss engine, processes content in Switzerland. The third-party engines, ‘DeepL Pro’, ‘Azure OpenAI GPT’ and ‘Claude’, are hosted abroad. Selecting one of them displays the ‘Attorney-Client privilege notice’, which requires the document to be fully pseudonymised and prohibits their use for a sensitive matter.
etapes: Open the engine list in Text and document translation and identify the one that is selected.
Remember that LexMachina processes content in Switzerland.
Remember that DeepL Pro, Azure OpenAI GPT and Claude are hosted abroad.
Read the ‘Attorney-Client privilege notice’ as soon as it appears: it signals processing outside Switzerland.
Fully pseudonymise the document before you send anything to a third-party engine, or go back to a Swiss engine.
savoir: The ‘Alternatives’ panel uses several engines to compare wordings: bear this in mind for confidential content.
‘Highly sensitive content’ mode is the simplest safeguard: it keeps storage and processing exclusively in Switzerland.
Third-party engines remain useful for neutral or already pseudonymised text, in particular to compare wordings.
articles.question: Which engines process my texts outside Switzerland?

articles.titre: Can I use a foreign engine for a matter covered by professional secrecy
articles.question: Can I use a foreign engine for a matter covered by professional secrecy?
articles.reponse: The app displays the Attorney-Client privilege notice as soon as a third-party engine is selected. Your organisation then requires you to remove any reference that could identify clients or the subject of the matter, and prohibits these engines for sensitive matters. For such matters, Highly sensitive content mode or the LexMachina engine keeps everything in Switzerland.

articles.titre: Is my content used to train models
articles.question: Is my content used to train the translation models?
articles.reponse: No. Client content is not used to train Neur.on's translation models. Projects created with Standard confidentiality can, however, feed a translation memory that only your organisation can reuse, and projects in Highly sensitive content mode are never reused.

articles.titre: Is Neur.on subject to the US CLOUD Act
articles.question: Is Neur.on subject to the US CLOUD Act?
articles.reponse: Neur.on AI Solutions SA is a company incorporated under Swiss law and based in Fribourg, and its infrastructure is hosted in Switzerland. Choosing a third-party engine hosted abroad, however, takes the text outside this scope, and the app warns you about this before anything is sent.

articles.title: Translation memories and reuse in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: Projects with standard confidentiality feed your own translation memory. In Highly sensitive content mode, no content is reused.
articles.reponse: In Corrext, projects created with ‘Standard confidentiality’ are saved on Corrext's Swiss servers. They can serve as a translation memory for your future projects, for the exclusive use of your organisation. Projects created with ‘Highly sensitive content’ are never reused as translation memory. You make the choice at the ‘Set-up’ step, when you create the project, and it applies to all its files.
etapes: At the Set-up step of a project, read the description of the two confidentiality cards before you choose.
Choose Standard confidentiality if you want the project to enrich your translation memory.
Choose Highly sensitive content so that no content is reused in future projects.
Check this choice before you upload your files: it applies to the whole project.
To view or manage the memories themselves, contact your administrator.
savoir: The memory built from your standard projects is used exclusively by your organisation: it is never shared with other clients.
Your administrator manages the organisation's memories: they can import memories in TMX format and term bases in TBX or XML format, up to 5 MB per file.
Not to be confused with CHnell, which searches collections of official texts, not your translation memory.
articles.question: How do translation memories work?

articles.titre: Log out and manage your account
articles.title: Log out and manage your Corrext account · Neur.on
articles.description: The avatar menu only contains Log out, and the bell shows your notifications. Changes to your user account go through your administrator.
articles.reponse: In the Corrext header, the avatar with your initials opens a menu that contains only ‘Log out’: this is where you end your session. The bell next to it shows your notifications, or ‘No notifications’ when there are none. No account settings page was observed from a standard user account: requests for changes go through your administrator.
etapes: Find the avatar with your initials at the far right of the header: it is on every screen.
Click it to open the menu, then choose Log out to end your session.
Click the bell next to the avatar to see your notifications.
To change your password, use the ‘Forgot your password ?’ link on the login screen.
For any other request (access rights, resources or memories), contact your administrator.
savoir: The avatar menu offers nothing but logging out: there is no profile page or preferences page on a standard user account.
User and rights management is not available from this type of account: ask your administrator.
Always log out on a shared computer: the documents you upload remain linked to your work session.
articles.question: How do I log out and manage my account?

h1: When Corrext does not do what you expect
lead: A greyed-out button, a missing language, a translation that does not start, a rejected file: four common problems, their exact cause in the app and how to fix them.
title: Corrext troubleshooting: buttons, languages, files · Neur.on
description: Next button inactive, target language missing, translation not starting, file rejected: the real causes of these problems and how to fix them.

articles.titre: The Next button stays greyed out
articles.title: Why the Next button stays greyed out in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: Next stays inactive until you choose a target language at the Set-up step, or until you upload a file at the File overview step.
articles.reponse: In Translation projects, the ‘Next’ button only becomes active once the current step is complete. At the ‘Set-up’ step, it stays greyed out until you select a target language. At the ‘File overview’ step, it stays greyed out until you upload a file. At the ‘Quotes’ step, the ‘Generate quote’ button follows the same logic and waits for a due date and a review level.
etapes: At the Set-up step, click ‘Select target languages’ and tick at least one target language.
Check that the language tag appears below the button: it is what activates ‘Next’.
At the File overview step, upload at least one file to the upload area before you look for ‘Next’.
At the Quotes step, enter a due date in ‘Due date’ and a level in ‘Review level’.
Then check that the Generate quote button has become active.
savoir: A greyed-out button in Corrext signals missing information, not a fault: the screen is always waiting for a specific entry.
If the language you want does not appear in the list, check the confidentiality level chosen at the previous step.
The project is created as soon as you move to the ‘File overview’ step, so you do not have to redo the initial set-up.
articles.question: Why is the Next button greyed out?

articles.titre: The target language is not available
articles.title: Why a target language is missing in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: In Highly sensitive content mode, Corrext limits the choice to German, French, Italian and English. Switch it off to get all 30 languages.
articles.reponse: If a target language does not appear in the list, the most common cause is ‘Highly sensitive content’ mode. This mode requires exclusively Swiss processing and is only available for German, French, Italian and English. If you switch it off, or choose standard confidentiality in a project, you get back the 30 languages of the platform.
etapes: In Text and document translation, find the Highly sensitive content toggle to the right of the tabs and check whether it is on.
Switch it off if your content allows it: the list of target languages reloads with all 30 languages.
In a project, go back to the Set-up step and check which confidentiality card is selected.
Choose Standard confidentiality if the document does not require exclusively Swiss processing.
If the content is confidential, keep sensitive mode and choose one of the four available languages.
savoir: The trade-off between confidentiality and language range is explicit in the app: the sensitive mode card itself lists its four languages.
Use the search field of the language list before you conclude that a language is missing: the list is long.
A missing language has nothing to do with the engine you chose: it is the confidentiality mode that restricts the list.
articles.question: Why is my target language not available?
