articles.title: Why the translation does not start in Corrext · Neur.on
articles.description: There is no Translate button: the text is translated as you type. Above all, check that the source and target languages are not the same.
articles.reponse: In the ‘Text translation’ tab, there is no button to start the translation: it happens as you type. If nothing appears in the right-hand pane, first check that the source and target languages are not the same. In that case, the app shows the message ‘Identical source and target languages’. A brief error message may also appear: try the action again.
etapes: Check that there is text in the left-hand pane and that the character counter is not at zero.
Compare the two language lists: if they are the same, the target pane shows Identical source and target languages.
Change the target language, or use the swap button between the two lists.
Check that you have not exceeded the character limit of the current tab.
If a brief error message appears, try the action again: the panel usually loads on the second attempt.
In CHnell, remember that the Enter key does not start the search: use the Search button.
savoir: There is deliberately no confirm button: the translation is recalculated each time the source text changes.
The regenerate button of the ‘Rephrasing’ tab is there precisely to ask for a new result when the first one is not suitable.
The same sentence may return an identical result after regeneration: this is the observed behaviour. In that case, use the ‘Alternatives’ panel.
articles.question: Why is my translation not starting?

articles.title: My file was rejected by Corrext: what to do · Neur.on
articles.description: A rejected file is almost always due to its format, a size over 50 MB or the number of files uploaded at once, which is limited to 25.
articles.reponse: When Corrext rejects a file, the cause is almost always one of three things: the format is not on the accepted list, the file is larger than 50 MB, or more than 25 files were uploaded at once. The ‘PDF to Word’ tab adds its own restriction, since it only accepts .pdf. The upload areas show these limits on screen, just below the upload button.
etapes: Check the extension: only .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx, .ppt and .pptx are accepted for translation.
Check that you are not on the PDF to Word tab, which only accepts .pdf.
Check the size of the file: the limit is 50 MB per file.
Count the files in your batch: the limit is 25 files per upload.
Start again from the original file, .docx or .xlsx rather than PDF: it is often smaller and better processed.
Read the text of the upload area, which shows the exact list of formats and the maximum size allowed.
savoir: Format and size are quicker to check than content: always start with these two points.
A very large scanned PDF should be converted to Word with the ‘PDF to Word’ tab before anything else.
The limits are the same in Text and document translation and in Translation projects: a file rejected by one will be rejected by the other.

h1: Manage the organisation, its members and their roles
lead: Add members, give them a role, bring in a whole team through its email domain and structure your organisation into child organisations.
title: Manage Corrext users and roles · Help Centre · Neur.on
description: Administering Corrext: the Admin, Project manager and Member roles, adding members, joining by email domain, parent and child organisations.

articles.titre: Which roles can be assigned in an organisation
articles.question: Which roles can I assign in an organisation?
articles.reponse: There are three roles in Corrext: Admin, Project manager and Member. You choose the role when you add a member, either individually or for a whole email domain.
savoir: The rights attached to each role are explained to you during set-up.
Who does this: your organisation's administrator.

articles.titre: How to add a member to the organisation
articles.question: How do I add a member to the organisation?
articles.reponse: The members of the organisation are listed in the ‘Direct memberships’ block, with their email address and role. The ‘Add member’ button adds an address and assigns it a role.
etapes: Open your organisation's members.
In Direct memberships, click Add member.
Enter the email address and choose the role: Admin, Project manager or Member.
Confirm: the person appears in the list with their role.
savoir: Who does this: your organisation's administrator.

articles.titre: How to add a whole team automatically
articles.question: How do I add a whole team automatically?
articles.reponse: The ‘Email domain memberships’ block links an entire email domain to a role, with the ‘Add domain’ button. Anyone who logs in with an address from that domain joins the organisation with that role.
savoir: Useful for a whole law firm or department: each new joiner is linked to the organisation as soon as they first log in.
Who does this: your organisation's administrator.

articles.titre: How to structure a parent company, subsidiaries or offices
articles.question: How do I set up a parent company with subsidiaries or offices?
articles.reponse: An organisation can have a parent organisation and child organisations, each with its own address or the address of the parent. Two settings are not passed on to child organisations: terminology activation and the confidentiality notice. They are set for each organisation.
savoir: Who does this: the Neur.on team, during set-up or on request.

h1: Decide on engines and the confidentiality notice
lead: Your organisation's engine policy: the engines allowed, the notice displayed before text is sent to a foreign engine, and the use of your own API keys.
title: Corrext: allowed engines and confidentiality · Neur.on
description: Administering Corrext: the engines allowed per organisation, the notice shown before foreign engines, and your own API keys for DeepL, Claude and GPT.

articles.titre: How to choose the engines available to our users
articles.question: How do we choose which engines our users can access?
articles.reponse: Each organisation has its own list of allowed engines (‘Allowed AI providers’). This is the organisation's engine policy: a department that handles sensitive matters can, for example, restrict itself to LexMachina.
savoir: In Highly sensitive content mode, only Swiss engines can be selected, whatever the list.
Who does this: the Neur.on team, during set-up or on request.

articles.titre: How to display a notice before text is sent to a foreign engine
articles.question: How do we display a notice before text is sent to a foreign engine?
articles.reponse: The ‘Show confidentiality warning when non-confidential engines are selected’ setting displays the Attorney-Client privilege notice as soon as a user chooses an engine hosted abroad. It is enabled organisation by organisation and is not passed on to child organisations.
savoir: The notice reminds users of your organisation's policy when they choose the engine, in the tool itself.
Who does this: the Neur.on team, during set-up or on request.

articles.titre: Can we use our own DeepL, Claude or GPT contracts
articles.question: Can we use our own DeepL, Claude or GPT contracts?
articles.reponse: Yes. By default, Corrext uses its own access keys for these engines. An organisation can provide its own API keys for DeepL, Claude and GPT, so that requests go through its own contracts with these providers.
savoir: Processing by these engines still takes place outside Switzerland: the confidentiality notice applies in the same way.
Who does this: the Neur.on team, during set-up or on request.

h1: Import your memories, term bases and resources
lead: Your organisation's own translation memories, term bases and CHnell resources, so that Corrext starts from your vocabulary.
title: Corrext translation memory and term base import · Neur.on
description: Administering Corrext: import TMX translation memories and TBX or XML term bases, and add your organisation's own resources to CHnell.

articles.titre: How to import our translation memories
articles.question: How do we import our translation memories?
articles.reponse: The organisation's memories are managed in ‘Manage translation memories’. The ‘Create’ button opens the import: first choose the categories, that is, the domains, then upload files in .tmx format, up to 5 MB per file.
savoir: Each memory remains linked to its domains, which you can change later in the list.
Who does this: your organisation's administrator, or the Neur.on team during set-up.

articles.titre: How to import a term base
articles.question: How do we import a term base?
articles.reponse: The organisation's term bases are managed in ‘Manage term bases’. The ‘Create’ button accepts .tbx or .xml files, up to 5 MB per file.
savoir: To set the translation of a term for one specific project, use that project's ‘Project terminology’ screen.
Who does this: your organisation's administrator, or the Neur.on team during set-up.

articles.titre: How to add our own resources to CHnell
articles.question: How do we add our own resources to CHnell?
articles.reponse: CHnell distinguishes shared resources, which come from official sources, from an organisation's own resources, which only that organisation can see. A document can be viewable in full or only as excerpts.
savoir: In search results, your resources are shown separately from the shared resources.
Who does this: the Neur.on team, during set-up or on request.
